title: Coverage of Long-Term Care (Medicare-Only Scenario)
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: Do either regular Medicare, Medicare Advantage Plans, or Medicare Supplement Plans cover long-term care?

accurate_complete: In general, none of these cover long-term custodial care
Although some time-limited nursing facility stays or in-home services may be covered in certain circumstances
OR: Clearly stated that none of these provide coverage for long-term care (without needing to elaborate on the limited exception)
accurate_incomplete: Some, but not all, relevant information was provided
Accurately raised the limited Medicare coverage that may be provided in certain situations that is similar to long-term care, without clarifying that Medicare does not actually cover long-term care
not_substantive: Counselor said they do not know or otherwise did not substantively answer the question
incorrect: Said that Medicare does cover long-term care without elaborating on the limited circumstances that apply (i.e., implied general long-term care coverage)

scoring_notes: This is one of the cleaner questions in the rubric — a clear 'no' answer with brief acknowledgment of the skilled nursing exception scores Accurate and Complete. The Incorrect condition is particularly important here: conflating short-term skilled nursing coverage with long-term custodial care is a material error that could lead a beneficiary to make a seriously incorrect coverage assumption.
